listsMenu.Name: Shop lists
listsMenu.Label: Edit the shop lists
listsMenu.Hint: The lists of items shops sell from: a smithy's, an alchemist's, a magic shop's. Fill them from the world's items or any compendium (homebrew and third-party ones too), paste in names copied from a book or a spreadsheet, add custom items, make starter lists from the Player's Handbook, or import a JSON file. Each item can have its own price, stock and shop level.

sellRate.Name: What shops pay
sellRate.Hint: What a shop pays for things players sell it, as a percentage of their price (50: half price). A shop can have its own in its settings.

sellApproval.Name: The GM approves sales
sellApproval.Hint: When a player sells something, it's sent to the GM as an offer: the GM can change the price (haggling) and approve it or turn it down. A GM must be logged in.

buyApproval.Name: The GM approves purchases
buyApproval.Hint: When a player buys something, it's sent to the GM as an offer first, as sales are.

playersCanSell.Name: Players can sell to shops
playersCanSell.Hint: Shops have a Sell tab where a player can sell their character's things.

receipts.Name: Receipts in chat
receipts.Hint: After each purchase or sale, a card in chat with what changed hands and for how much.
receipts.Private: Only for the character's owners and the GM

gmDoubleClick.Name: The GM opens shops by double-clicking too
gmDoubleClick.Hint: Double-clicking a shop's token opens the shop for the GM as well as for players. Hold Alt to open the actor's sheet instead. Turn this off to open the sheet as usual (the Shop button on the Token HUD still opens the shop).

offersPopup.Name: Open offers as they come in
offersPopup.Hint: When a player sends an offer, the offers window opens (for the GM). Off: a notification instead.

Reasons.hiddenHint: You took this out of this shop. Players don't see it.
Reasons.levelHint: It needs a shop of level {level}; this one is level {shop}. Players don't see it.
Reasons.priceHint: It costs more than this shop's highest price ({price}). Players don't see it.
Reasons.noPriceHint: It has no price, so it can't be bought. Give it one in the shop lists. Players don't see it.
Reasons.notPickedHint: It wasn't in this shop's random pick. Reroll for a new pick. Players don't see it.

Shop.NoTrader: You have no character to trade with.
Shop.StockHint: How many this shop has left. Empty: back to its list's stock.
Shop.StockInvalid: Stock must be a whole number, or empty.
Shop.SellApprovalNote: The GM approves sales, and may name another price.
Shop.SellNote: This shop pays {n}% of an item's price.
Shop.ShopShort: {name} hasn't the coins to pay for it all.
Shop.LevelHint: The highest rarity this shop sells
Shop.EmptyGM: This shop has nothing to sell. Give it a shop list in its settings, or let it sell the shopkeeper's own items.
Shop.RestockHint: Every item back to its full stock (rolled stocks rolled again).
Shop.RerollHint: A new random pick of what the shop has, and restocked.
Shop.ShowAllHint: Show what players don't see too (hidden, above the shop's level, not picked).

Offers.Title: Offers
Offers.PriceHint: The price for one, in gold pieces (or "5 sp"). Change it to haggle.
Offers.ApprovedBuy: The GM approved: {name} bought it for {total}.
Offers.ApprovedSell: The GM approved: {name} sold it for {total}.

Errors.NoTrader: There's no character to trade with.
Errors.ItemMissing: The item {name} is made from can't be found.
Errors.NotInInventory: That isn't in the inventory any more.
Errors.NotBought: This shop doesn't buy things like {name}.
Errors.GMOnly: Only the GM can do that.
Errors.OfferGone: That offer has already been answered.
Errors.NoGM: A GM must be logged in to trade.
Errors.GMTimeout: The GM's client didn't answer in time.
Errors.GMFailed: The GM's client couldn't make the trade.

Config.Title: Shop settings: {name}
Config.SetupHint: Make this actor a shop. Every token of it opens the same shop.
Config.Name: Shop name
Config.GreetingHint: What the shopkeeper says when someone comes in.
Config.OpenHint: Players can trade here. A closed shop can still be looked in.
Config.RangeHint: How close a player's token must be to the shop's token, or to one of its map pins, to trade. Empty: from anywhere.
Config.RibbonHint: How this shop's ribbons look, hanging at the top of the screen.
Config.NoLists: There are no shop lists yet.
Config.LevelHint: The highest rarity it sells: a level 2 shop sells mundane, common and uncommon items. An item can have its own level in the shop lists.
Config.MaxPriceHint: Leave out anything dearer than this. Empty: no limit.
Config.RandomHint: The shop has only so many items of each rarity, picked at random from its lists (empty: all of them). Make a new pick from the shop window.
Config.SellOwnHint: Things in the shopkeeper's inventory that aren't equipped are for sale too, as many as they have.
Config.MarkupHint: What this shop charges, as a percentage of an item's price (120: a fifth dearer).

Buys.same: Only the kinds of thing it sells

Config.SellRateHint: What it pays for things, as a percentage of their price. Empty: the world's setting.
Config.KeepBoughtHint: Things players sell go back on the shelves: into the stock of what the shop sells already, else into the shopkeeper's inventory (and for sale, if it sells its own items).
Config.PurseHint: What it pays comes out of the shopkeeper's coins, and what it's paid goes in. Off: it has coins without end.
Config.RemoveText: {name} won't be a shop any more. Its settings, stock and offers waiting are deleted.

Lists.Title: Shop lists
Lists.NoLists: There are no shop lists yet. Make one, make starter lists from your item compendiums, or import some.
Lists.BrowserFailed: The Compendium Browser couldn't be opened.
Lists.RefreshHint: Read each item's name, picture, price and rarity again (after a compendium changed). What you set here stays.
Lists.DropHint: Drop items, folders of items or whole compendiums here to add them.
Lists.DropEmpty: There are no items you can carry in it.
Lists.DropOnlyItems: Drop items, folders of items or item compendiums.
Lists.CheckHint: Tick items to change many at once.
Lists.ClearPricesHint: Back to the item's own price.
Lists.Name: Item
Lists.SortHint: Sort by this; again for the other way.
Lists.PriceHint: Its price in these shops, in gold pieces ("2.5", or coins: "5 sp", "1 gp 5 sp"). Empty: the item's own price. A shop's markup is on top.
Lists.StockHint: How many a shop has: a number, or a roll such as 1d4+1 (rolled when the shop is stocked and each restock). Empty: no limit.
Lists.LevelHint: The shop level it needs: 0 mundane, 1 common, 2 uncommon, 3 rare, 4 very rare, 5 legendary, 6 artifact. By rarity unless you set one (a mundane spyglass a village shop shouldn't have: 3).
Lists.NoEntries: No items yet. Add some with the buttons above, or drop them here.
Lists.Missing: The item this was made from can't be found. It can't be bought until it's back, or you remove it and add it again.
Lists.BadPrice: "{text}" isn't a price. Try 25, 2.5, 5 sp or 1 gp 5 sp.
Lists.BadStock: "{text}" isn't a stock. Try 3, 1d4 or 2d6+1, or leave it empty for no limit.
Lists.AddedDup: Added {n} ({dup} were on the list already).
Lists.PasteHint: One item per line: its name, then if you like its price, stock and shop level, split by tabs, | or ;. Copy a table from a book, a document or a spreadsheet. Names are looked up in the world's items and the item compendiums; an item on the list already gets the new price, stock and level.
Lists.PasteEverywhere: The world and every item compendium
Lists.PasteCustom: Add names not found as custom items
Lists.PasteDone: {found} found and added, {custom} added as custom items, {updated} updated.
Lists.NotFoundText: {n} names weren't found, and weren't added:
Lists.CustomNoName: A custom item needs a name.

CustomFields.Name: Name
CustomFields.PriceHint: In gold pieces (25, 2.5), or coins (5 sp, 1 gp 5 sp).
CustomFields.BundleHint: How many are sold as one (arrows by 20).
CustomFields.StockHint: A number, or a roll such as 1d4. Empty: no limit.

Lists.StarterHint: Make shop lists from item compendiums: everything with a price, sorted into a general store's, a smithy's, an alchemist's, a magic shop's, a scribe's and a toolmaker's. Where a name is in two compendiums, the first one ticked wins. A list with the same name as one you have is replaced.
Lists.StarterNone: No items with a price were found there.
Lists.StarterDone: {n} lists made, with {entries} items. Save to keep them.
Lists.ImportHint: A JSON file of shop lists (exported from Primal Shops, or written by hand: a list is { "name": "…", "entries": [ … ] }, and an entry can be a line such as "Longsword | 15"). Pick a file from Foundry's files or your computer, or paste it in.
Lists.ImportDone: {added} lists added and {replaced} replaced, with {entries} items. Save to keep them.

Pins.RangeHint: How close a player's token must be to this pin to trade, when they have a token on this scene (with none, they can trade from anywhere). Empty: the shop's own range ({range}).
Pins.RemoveConfirm: Take {name}'s pin off this scene? The shop itself stays as it is.
Pins.Placed: {name}'s pin is on the map, hidden from players. Right-click it to reveal it, and drag it to move it.
Pins.DropQuestion: Put {name} on the map as a token or a map pin, or hang it as a ribbon at the top of the screen?
Pins.Place: Place a pin on this scene
Pins.PlaceHint: Both go on the scene you're viewing, hidden until you right-click them and reveal them. A pin goes in the middle of your view, and players double-click it. A ribbon hangs from the top of the screen, and players click it to trade from anywhere on the scene.

Ribbons.Place: Hang a ribbon on this scene
Ribbons.Placed: {name}'s ribbon hangs at the top of the screen, hidden from players. Right-click it to reveal it.
Ribbons.Already: {name} has a ribbon on this scene already.
Ribbons.RemoveConfirm: Take down {name}'s ribbon on this scene? The shop itself stays as it is.

New.Title: New shop
New.NoLists: No shop lists yet. Make some in the Shop lists window (Game Settings, Primal Shops) to stock it, or make it now and fill it later.
New.Name: Name

Place.ribbon: As a ribbon at the top of the screen
Place.pin: As a pin in the middle of your view

New.Link: Open it from the selected tokens too: {names}
New.Made: {name} is made. It's in the Shops folder of the Actors sidebar: drop it on a map to put it on a scene.
New.MadeRibbon: {name} is made, and its ribbon hangs at the top of the screen for everyone.
New.MadeRibbonHidden: {name} is made, and its ribbon hangs at the top of the screen, hidden from players. Right-click it to reveal it.
New.MadePin: {name} is made, and its pin is on the map for everyone.
New.MadePinHidden: {name} is made, and its pin is on the map, hidden from players. Right-click it to reveal it.

Link.Unlink: Unlink its {n} tokens on this scene
Link.Hint: Linked tokens open this shop when double-clicked, whatever they are: a merchant, a market stall, a signpost. Select them on the map first.
Link.NoneSelected: Select the tokens on the map first (not players' own).

Here.Title: Shops here: {scene}
Here.None: No shops here that you know of.
Here.NoneGM: No shops on this scene yet. Drop a shop's actor on the map to place a token, a pin or a ribbon.
